scope: Supplemental practice for Music for Mimes. Use the teacher’s directions for your assigned performance.

pool.prompt: You close an invisible drawer. What helps the audience recognize it as the same drawer you opened?
options: Close it at the same height and location.
Reach above your head when you close it.
Look somewhere else when you open it.
Use a different grip every time.
pool.rationale: Keeping the object in a consistent place makes it readable.

pool.prompt: What is the clearest way to show an invisible cup resting on a table?
options: Lower it all the way to the floor.
Set it down at the same height where you picked it up.
Let it vanish as soon as you stop drinking.
Move it without shaping your hand around it.
pool.rationale: The height and grip help the audience picture the cup and table.

pool.prompt: What makes an invisible suitcase easiest to follow after you put it down?
options: Reach in a new direction without moving it.
Describe it to the audience aloud.
Look and reach back to the same place when you pick it up again.
Change its size each time you touch it.
pool.rationale: Consistent position tells the audience the suitcase stayed where you left it.

pool.prompt: Which movement best shows you just found out a box is heavy?
options: Swing it up quickly with one finger.
Lift it easily while looking at the ceiling.
Keep your posture and speed exactly the same.
Brace your feet and lift slowly with visible effort.
pool.rationale: Visible effort, stance, and slower timing suggest resistance.

pool.prompt: Which movement most clearly shows a jammed zipper?
options: Hold the fabric steady and make two short pulls that meet resistance.
Wave both hands above your head.
Slide your hand smoothly without pausing.
Turn around before touching the zipper.
pool.rationale: The repeated pull and resistance show a specific problem.

pool.prompt: What best communicates that an object became easier to carry?
options: Change where the object is without showing a move.
Change from slow, braced steps to lighter steps while keeping the same grip.
Look away and stop interacting with it.
Walk at the same speed with the same effort.
pool.rationale: A deliberate change in effort and pace helps the audience see a difference in weight.

pool.prompt: The music goes from quick to slow. Which choice makes the change clear?
options: Keep the same pace for the whole piece.
Explain the change out loud.
Move from light, quick steps to slower, deliberate steps.
Change your costume without changing your movement.
pool.rationale: Changing the movement’s speed helps the audience see the musical contrast.

pool.prompt: Why might you pause right after the music changes?
options: To make the invisible object change locations.
To add dialogue to the scene.
To make the ending happen before the problem.
To give the audience time to notice your reaction.
pool.rationale: A purposeful pause can draw attention to a moment or reaction.

pool.prompt: The music grows more energetic as your character spots a friend. What action best fits that moment?
options: Use a quicker step and an open, eager gesture.
Keep a slow walk and hide your face.
Start moving a different imaginary object.
Turn your back without showing a reaction.
pool.rationale: A change in pace and gesture can show the character’s excitement.

pool.prompt: Which sequence has a clear beginning, middle, and end?
options: Open a bag, then begin an unrelated action, then freeze.
Spot the bag, struggle with its zipper, then open it and react.
React to the zipper before showing the bag, then stop.
Stand holding a bag with no goal or change.
pool.rationale: The viewer sees the goal, the problem, and the outcome.

pool.prompt: A viewer saw the start and ending but missed the obstacle. What should you revise?
options: Add a new object after the ending.
Repeat the same motions at the same speed.
Make the moment of resistance and your reaction clearer.
Explain the entire scene before performing it.
pool.rationale: Revise the moment that the audience could not read.

pool.prompt: What is a good way to check if your silent scene communicated the story?
options: Tell the viewer every detail first.
Ask only whether the music was loud enough.
Assume everyone understood because no one asked a question.
Ask the viewer what goal and problem they saw before explaining.
pool.rationale: An unprompted description shows which parts of the performance were clear.
